In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the work presented in this paper is the first demonstration of a fully autonomous vision-based quadrotor perching on a line using a monocular camera.
we show that it is possible to use a small quadrotor to perch on arbitrarily oriented line using only a monocular camera.
we show that a quadrotor can be controlled using a single camera to perch on a target line, without the need for any prior knowledge about the line orientation or the robot's position.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that it is possible to use a monocular camera for perching on arbitrary lines, and that we can do so with a lightweight and inexpensive micro-quadrotor.
we are able for the first time to control a quadrotor to perch on a line in a fully autonomous fashion, using only the camera and IMU.
the quadrotor is able to fly above and land on arbitrarily oriented lines without any external sensor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use only features on planes and arbitrarily oriented lines to control a quadrotor in order to perch on a line.
it is possible to control a robot using a monocular camera without relying on the 3D structure of the environment, which is very difficult to estimate in practice.
the robot can compute its position and orientation with respect to the line, its velocity, the velocity of the line and its orientation without using a priori information on the environment.
